unmapped_findings: For M2-SS, no κ-carbides are quantified (Table 3 shows a dash for κ in M2-SS); only (Ti,V)C carbides are present (2.4 ± 1.4 %, mean radius 35.8 ± 20.1 nm).

The addition of Ti and V does not alter the austenitic phase composition of the low-density steel but refines the grain size; the M2-SS grain size is 32.3 ± 10.4 μm versus 42.4 ± 7.8 μm for the Ti/V-free M1-SS.

(Ti,V)C carbides are high-temperature precipitates (precipitation temperatures of Ti and V exceed 1000 °C) that form before aging and remain stable, so their size and volume fraction do not change under aging.
The calculated SFE of M2 (≈78 mJ/m²) indicates the deformation mode of the material is dislocation slip, consistent with TEM observations of planar slip.

Fig. 10 (strengthening mechanism bar chart) indicates M2-SS measured yield strength lies between 600 and 800 MPa, with calculated contributions σ0 + σG + σOr (no κ shear strengthening σS); however no numeric labels are printed on the chart.

The two solution-treated steels (M1-SS and M2-SS) were produced by the same process (proc_ss-1000c-30min) but differ in composition; M2-SS exhibits ~200 MPa higher yield strength than M1-SS due to (Ti,V)C precipitation.
